title: Multispectral Imaging Protocol for Myeloid Cell Heterogeneity in Cryosections
author: Wieland, Kempen, et al.

steps.title: Cut tissue sections
steps.instruction: After tissue collection and embedding in Optimal Cutting Temperature (OCT) medium, use a cryostat to cut sequential cryosections.

steps.title: Prepare antibody spectral library
steps.instruction: Select a panel of antibodies conjugated to dyes that share excitation wavelengths but have distinct emission spectra, titrate each antibody, and assemble the resulting spectra into a spectral library for multiplex imaging.

steps.title: Stain and acquire multiplex images
steps.instruction: Stain the cryosections with the prepared antibody‑dye panel, acquire the multi‑marker fluorescent image in a single‑shot acquisition, then perform H&E staining on the same section to enable histopathological evaluation and later cell segmentation.

steps.title: Prepare blocking buffer (PBS + 4% FCS)
steps.instruction: Mix 2 mL fetal calf serum (FCS) with 48 mL 1× PBS, filter the solution through a 0.2 µm filter, and store at 4 °C for up to two weeks.

substeps.instruction: Measure 2 mL FCS.
Add 48 mL 1× PBS.
Filter through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Label and store at 4 °C (max 2 weeks).

steps.title: Align H&E with fluorescent images
steps.instruction: Use the AutoRegi_Nuance_HE MATLAB app to align the H&E image with the fluorescent (7‑AAD) image, ensuring alignment precision of ≤5 µm.

substeps.instruction: Download ‘AutoRegi_Nuance_HE.mlapp’ from GitHub.
Install the app in MATLAB (ensure the Image Processing Toolbox is added).
Run the app; a pop‑up window appears.
Click “load” and open the 7‑AAD fluorescent image and the corresponding H&E image from the same tissue section.
In the ‘manually’ panel, select ‘selectpoint’ and click ‘run’ to open the side‑by‑side view.
Place a crosshair on a recognizable landmark in one image, then click the matching point in the other image; repeat for at least five landmarks spread across the field of view.
Optionally click the two‑landmark icon to let the script predict additional points and adjust them manually if needed.
Verify that the overlay is accurate (≤5 µm error).
Close the pop‑up; the main window now shows the merged image.
Save the cropped, aligned H&E image as ‘HE.jpg’.
Optionally save the transformation matrix (tform.mat) or landmark file via the ‘save panel’.
For future alignments, you may load a previously saved landmark file or tform.mat using ‘alignwithpoint’ or ‘alignwithtform’.
Alternatively, switch to the ‘auto’ panel, adjust image‑processing parameters for both channels, and run automatic registration (may be slower depending on computer and image size).

steps.title: Segment cells in QuPath
steps.instruction: Detect individual cells on the aligned H&E image using QuPath and export the segmentation mask for fluorescence quantification.

substeps.instruction: Open QuPath.
Load the aligned H&E image (HE.jpg) and set the image type to Brightfield (H&E).
Define the region of interest (whole image or exclude artifacts).
Choose Analyze > Cell detection > Cell detection.
In the settings window, turn off ‘include cell nucleus’ and adjust parameters until all cells are correctly segmented.
Copy the segmentation to ImageJ via Extensions > ImageJ > Send region to ImageJ.
In ImageJ, save the mask as a ROI set: Image > Overlay > to ROI manager → select all ROIs → save as ‘RoiSet.zip’ in the same folder.
Overlay the ROI mask onto each fluorescent image (Image > Overlay > from ROI manager) to enable per‑cell intensity measurement.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence per cell
steps.instruction: Using CellProfiler, ImageJ, QuPath, or another image‑analysis tool, measure the mean intensity of each dye within every segmented cell, compile the data into a (co‑)expression matrix, and proceed to downstream heterogeneity analysis.
